# Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item tab existence

## Problem statement

The "in progress" marker shown in the Herdr selection list is unreliable: it is
derived from the worklog `in-progress` status, which is maintained by the
hydrator — a self-healing loop that decides whether a claimed item is genuinely
being worked on by matching the item ID against live **pane titles**
(`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`). That pane-title matching predates the
one-tab-per-work-item convention: every interactive/downtime dispatch now places
its agent pane in a tab labelled with the **exact work-item ID**
(`getItemTabAnchor` / `findTabByLabel` in `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts`).
Panes can be re-parented, renamed, truncated or multi-pane per tab, so pane-title
matching produces false negatives (→ wrong demotion, marker disappears while work
continues) and is needlessly complex.

## Users

- Herdr operator selecting the next work item from the selection list.
- Downtime dispatcher / plugin panes that rely on the hydrator to release stale
  `in-progress` claims so the item re-enters the dispatchable pool.

Example user stories:

- As a Herdr operator, I want the selection list's in-progress marker to reflect
  reality — an item is "being worked on" iff a tab named after its work-item ID
  exists in my workspace — so I can trust the list without opening tabs.
- As a dispatched agent, I want my claimed item left `in-progress` for as long as
  my work-item tab is open, so my claim is never released underneath me.
- As an operator, I want a stale claim (no work-item tab) released automatically
  and periodically so abandoned items return to the dispatchable pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a tab in the current workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`) has a label **equal to** the work-item ID; a tab label that merely *contains* the ID does not count, and a pane title containing the ID no longer counts on its own. Verified by unit tests over a pure tab-matching helper.
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is switched from `herdr pane list` + pane-title ID extraction to `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` + exact tab label match; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`, `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are replaced by tab equivalents. Verified by code review + updated `hydrator.test.ts` (no `pane list` spawn asserted).
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` → `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An item with a matching tab is never demoted. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing 30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible focus-resume hook both re-evaluate tab existence, so a closed work-item tab clears the marker within one cadence and an opened tab keeps it. Verified by existing scheduler/visibility tests plus a tab-based hydration test.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr tab list` aborts the cycle without demoting, and tabs outside the current workspace never mark an item active. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (notably the hydrator module header, `pane-title.ts` rationale comment and `herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` if it references pane-title matching).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the worklog status/stage vocabulary or the demotion outcome rules.
- Keep the bounded/responsive hydrator contract (per-step timeout, per-tick cap,
  stdio isolation, fail-open) unchanged; only the "which items are active" lookup
  changes.
- Reuse the existing tab listing/parsing (`listTabsInWorkspace`,
  `parseTabListOutput`, `findTabByLabel`) rather than adding a second parser.
- Retain exports still used elsewhere: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
  (`ship-guard.ts`) and `isActiveBlocker` (`stalled-work.ts`).
- No CLI or socket API change; `herdr tab list` is already used by the plugin.
- Write in UK English; follow the project's test/build conventions.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — fetches `wl list --status in-progress`,
  fetches `herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]`, collects work-item IDs from pane
  labels (`WORK_ITEM_ID_REGEX` over `pane.label`), and demotes items with no
  matching pane. Exposes pure helpers (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`,
  `isActivePaneMatch`, `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — creates the hydrator runner with
  `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, runs it every 30 s (`hydrate`
  task) and on hidden→visible focus-resume. The selection list's in-progress
  marker (`statusIcon(item.status)`) and Group N ordering (`status ===
  'in-progress'`) are driven by the worklog status this loop maintains.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — already lists/creates tabs labelled
  with the exact item ID: `listTabsInWorkspace`, `parseTabListOutput`,
  `findTabByLabel`, `getItemTabAnchor`.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — truncation helper exists specifically so
  the ID survives in pane titles for the hydrator; this rationale becomes obsolete
  for matching (the helper may remain for human-readable titles).

## Desired change

Replace the hydrator's pane-title-based "is this item active" signal with a
tab-label-based one:

1. Add a pure helper that, given the tabs of the current workspace, returns the
   set of work-item IDs whose tab label matches exactly (e.g.
   `collectTabWorkItemIds(tabs)` / `hasItemTab(itemId, tabs)`).
2. Change `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes` → `listTabs(workspaceId)` backed by
   `herdr tab list --workspace <id>` (reusing the shared parser), and update
   `runHydrationOnce` to use tab membership.
3. Keep `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`,
   `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` and the bounded-run machinery intact.
4. Update tests and the module/doc comments to describe tab-based detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — replace pane matching with exact tab-label matching; rename seam/types/helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.ts` — reuse/export `listTabsInWorkspace` / `parseTabListOutput` / `findTabByLabel` for the hydrator's tab lookup.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring (workspace id, cadence, focus-resume); update comments if needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — rewrite active-pane cases as active-tab cases; add exact-match, workspace-scope and fail-open cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts` — replace `makeWorstCasePanes` with tab fixtures and update the exec router to answer `tab list`.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — update to the tab-based deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — adjust/retire the "hydrator matches pane titles" rationale comment.
- `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` — update if it documents pane-title matching for the hydrator.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI — Herdr hydrator: rescue `in_progress` work items with no active pane (parent of the pane-matching design).
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale `in_progress` items (child, currently blocked).
- WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ / WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO / WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX — bounded/isolated hydrate steps (contract to preserve).
- WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI / WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — item-ID tab anchor and interactive dispatch wiring (the tab-per-item convention this builds on).
- WL-0MUY1CS9E006ZLS0 — re-based Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on `status` (the marker this work makes reliable).
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — per-row agent-status icon (separate, richer herdr agent-reporting signal; out of scope here).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLX5OADB1TECIZV** – Testing: automation - create work item (completed)
- **WL-0MM0DTK1B1Z0VMIB** – wl list --stage in_review returns nothing while --json shows content (completed)
- **WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN** – Herdr: re-enable terminal drag-select while keeping mouse support (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, existence, herdr (+17 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, existence, herdr (+17 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: base, carries, detection, herdr, iff (+15 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "the logic for discovering when an item is being worked
  on" is the hydrator's active detection; the selection-list in-progress marker
  follows from the status the hydrator maintains. The agent-status icon
  (`AgentTracker`, herdr `agent list`) is a distinct feature and is not changed.
- **Assumption:** tabs are labelled with the exact work-item ID
  (`getItemTabAnchor` / `findTabByLabel` convention), so exact label equality is
  the correct match; substring matching is rejected to avoid false positives.
- **Assumption:** `herdr tab list` returns `result.tabs[].label` (and `tab_id`),
  as parsed by `parseTabListOutput`; no new herdr capability is required.
- **Risk:** legacy tabs created before the item-ID convention (or hand-created
  tabs) may not be labelled with the ID, so an item could be demoted while a
  legacy pane is still active. Mitigation: the item-ID tab convention is now the
  only dispatch path; document the change.
- **Risk:** a tab may outlive its agent (kept open after the agent finishes),
  leaving an item `in-progress`. This matches the requested rule (tab = worked
  on); operators close the tab to release the item.
- **Scope-creep risk:** sharing the signal with `AgentTracker` or the agent-status
  icon. Record any such opportunity as a linked follow-up work item, not in scope
  here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which 'logic for discovering when an item is being worked on' should switch
  to tab existence: the hydrator's stale-claim detection, or a new
  display-layer marker?" — **Assumed answer** (Map, from the intake seed): the
  hydrator's stale-claim detection, whose status output drives the selection-list
  in-progress marker. Evidence: `hydrator.ts` is the only discovery logic
  (pane-title matching predating per-item tabs); the worklist runs it every 30 s
  and on focus-resume. Source: interactive intake request; recorded as an
  assumption for producer confirmation at review.
- Q: "Does tab 'matching the work item ID' mean exact label equality or
  contains?" — **Assumed answer** (Map): exact equality, consistent with
  `findTabByLabel` ("never a substring/prefix match") and `getItemTabAnchor`
  (tab labelled exactly the item ID). Source: repo inspection.
- Q: "Should a matching tab require a live pane inside it?" — **Assumed answer**
  (Map): no — tab existence is the signal, per the seed request ("If there is a
  tab ... then it is being worked on"). Source: interactive intake request.

## Plan (decomposition)

Planned 2026-10-10. Three child work items, created in dependency order:

1. **WL-0MV24RM9I0051GEF** — Hydrator: switch active detection to exact tab-label
   matching (core + test migration). Vertical slice: `hydrator.ts` types, pure
   helpers, orchestration and production wiring, plus the structural test/fixture
   migration needed to keep the package green.
2. **WL-0MV24T2VJ007Q49J** — Verification: tab-matching edge cases (exact match,
   substring rejection, workspace scoping, fail-open, no pane-list spawn) plus
   the responsiveness-suite migration. Depends on the core item.
3. **WL-0MV25EE4E0028KDI** — Docs: hydrator module header, `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`,
   `packages/herdr/README.md` and the `pane-title.ts` rationale comment. Depends on
   the core item.

Test-first: the core item follows TDD (tab-matching tests written/extended before
the implementation); the verification item adds the exhaustive behavioural
coverage demanded by this item's ACs.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-10 — Created the three child items above and wired the dependency
  edges (verification → core; docs → core).
- 2026-10-10 — Reformatted the multi-line acceptance-criteria bullets into
  single-line bullets so automated AC-coverage extraction works (no intent
  change; the prior line wrapping truncated every AC to its first line).
data.title: Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item tab existence

## Summary

Vitest additions covering drag-to-scroll in the Herdr worklist list and detail views, written before implementation (test-first). Covers parent ACs 1–6: threshold dead-zone, list drag rows + selection invariance, detail drag lines + clamping, drag-release inert, hover on button-less motion, drag inert in filter mode, and the updated motion-branch tests for the hover-vs-drag split.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Suite exercises a pure `mapMouseDrag(state, ev, dragState, termSize)` returning `drag-start` / `drag-list` / `drag-detail` / null, including the threshold dead-zone where movement at or below `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS` is inert (parent AC5)
- Suite covers list drag: left-button-held vertical motion past the threshold yields `drag-list` with whole-row deltas proportional to movement, and `WorkItemListState.scrollBy` changes `scrollOffset` while `selectedIndex` is unchanged (parent AC1)
- Suite covers detail drag: the same gesture in detail mode yields `drag-detail` with 1 terminal row ≈ 1 line, clamped to the content bounds via the existing detail scroll clamp (parent AC2)
- Suite covers drag-vs-click isolation: a press that crosses the threshold yields no `select-row`/`open-detail`, its release is inert, and a press–release that never crosses the threshold still selects (or double-clicks) as before (parent AC3)
- Suite covers hover/drag separation: button-less motion (`(button & 3) === 3`) maps to `hover-row`/`hover-none` while left-button-held motion maps to drag (parent AC4)
- Suite covers threshold/clamping edges: sub-threshold drags are inert; drags past the content bounds clamp at 0/max without overscroll or selection movement (parent AC5)
- Suite covers filter-mode inertness: drag motion in filter mode yields null (out of scope)
- New tests live in `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts`; the existing motion-branch guard tests are updated to reflect the hover-vs-drag split, and the suite runs green via the herdr vitest run

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` with drag describe blocks, following the existing pure-function test pattern (`press`, `TERM_80x24`, `makeListState` fixtures)
- Add a `dragState` test helper mirroring `MouseClickState`; assert on the mapper's return value and on state effects after `handleMouseInput`
- Update the existing "drag-motion guard and button codes" describe block so motion coverage reflects hover (button-less) vs drag (left-held)

## Dependencies

None — created first (test-first ordering).

## Deliverables

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` additions (new + updated drag tests)
- Red-phase evidence recorded as a comment on the parent

### Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (contract under test)

data.description:
Discovered during WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6 (discovered-from:WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6).

## Problem
`implement.py finish`'s test gate failed twice with a spurious 'live-repo mutation detected' verdict even though the canonical suite passed (both declared commands exited 0). The guard (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` `snapshot_repo_state`/`diff_snapshots`, used by `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:guarded_run_all`) snapshots refs, local `.git/config`, registered worktrees, and `git status` before/after the suite. On a multi-agent host with several active worktrees, concurrent agent activity moved:
- `refs/remotes/origin/dev` (observed bbc8e89a -> 4163175)
- `refs/heads/dev` (main checkout's local dev, advanced by another agent's finish fast-forward)
- another agent's feature branch ref

Only refs checked out in agent worktrees under `.worklog/worktrees/` (and their `branch.<name>.*` config) are excluded, so these deltas fail the gate.

## Impact
`implement.py finish` fails after a ~17-minute suite run and resets the item to `open`; the agent must sync its worktree to the latest `dev` and re-warm the test cache before retrying. Observed twice on WL-0MV4VQ78L003TGY6.

## Possible fix
Exclude `refs/heads/dev`, `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and `refs/remotes/origin/*` (or ignore ref movement entirely) from the mutation diff while still catching working-tree mutations caused by the suite itself; or scope the ref check to refs the suite could plausibly touch.

## Workaround
Fast-forward the worktree to the latest `origin/dev`, run the full suite once to warm the per-command cache, then re-run `implement.py finish` (cache hits shrink the race window).
data.title: Finish-gate live-repo guard trips on concurrent dev ref movement in multi-agent repos

data.description:
The Herdr worklist selection list calls wl next to populate its results. wl next excludes dependency-blocked items by default (filterCandidates removes them unless includeBlocked is true). This means the Herdr selection list never shows dependency-blocked items, even though the user may need to see what is blocking their backlog.

Acceptance Criteria:
1. The Herdr worklist selection list includes dependency-blocked items alongside open and in-progress items.
2. Blocked items are rendered with a visible indicator (status icon) so their state is clear.
3. The change is confined to the fetchNextItems invocation in fetcher.ts - no other callers of wl next are affected.
4. Unit tests cover the new --include-blocked flag in the args array.

Notes:
The change adds --include-blocked to the wl next args in fetchNextItems() (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts). status=blocked items were already included by wl next (the pipeline only penalises them with -10000); the gap is dependency-blocked items that are excluded entirely. Blocked items will rank low (penalised) by default scoring, so they appear at the bottom of the list.
data.title: Herdr selection list should show dependency-blocked items
